raw_case_text:
A 30-year-old housewife presented with multiple, large, ulcerative lesions all over the body of 1-month duration. She did not give any history of genital lesions before the onset of skin lesions. Concomitant symptoms of headache, fever, myalgia and leucorrhea were present. She also gave a history of two spontaneous miscarriages for which she had not taken treatment and has not had contact with her husband since 6 months. Her husband, a lorry driver had multiple extra and premarital contacts. He was diagnosed as having HIV 2 years ago and was initiated on antiretroviral therapy. He was currently being treated for chancroid as well, due to many genital ulcers that he presented to us with.
On examination, the patient was febrile. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple, ulcerative, crusted lesions on the face and extremities [Figures 1 and 2]. Erosions were present on the lips and genital mucosa as well. Palms [Figure 3] and soles showed multiple annular lesions with central pigmentation. The axillary, epitrochlear and inguinal lymph nodes were enlarged, tender and rubbery in consistency.
Initial laboratory investigations revealed leucocytosis, with predominance of polymorphs and an elevated ESR. VDRL was reactive (1:128 dilution) and HIV-1 was positive (ELISA). Western blot assay for P24 antigen was also found to be positive. Pus culture from the ulcerated lesions grew Staphylococcus aureus which was highly sensitive to newer quinolones. CSF analysis showed no abnormalities of raised intracranial pressure, pleocytosis or elevated proteins. CSF VDRL was nonreactive in our patient.
VDRL of the patient's partner was found to be positive in 1:64 dilution. We initiated treatment with Benzathine penicillin G 24 lakh units intramuscularly as a single dose following which the partner was lost to follow-up.
Skin biopsy of the rupioid lesions showed pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with ulceration, dense lymphocytic infiltrate at mid-dermal level on 20x magnification [Figure 4] and plasma cell infiltrate with obliterative vasculitis on 40x magnification [Figure 5].
Since the patient gave history of intense headache and fever we considered an impending CNS involvement and hence treatment was initiated with procaine penicillin 1.2 million units daily for 3 weeks intramuscularly, and we also took the advantage of admitting the patient in our hospital. She was also given a course of oral antibiotics to eliminate the S. aureus. Patient started responding to treatment and all her cutaneous lesions healed completely in 3 weeks [Figures 6 and 7]. Patient also showed leukoderma colli around her neck. She was discharged and referred to a HIV center for HAART therapy. Monthly VDRL titers were done, and there was a four-fold decrease in the titers. Follow-up after 6 months showed no evidence of relapse, with a nonreactive VDRL and positive TPHA.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old housewife presented with a 1-month history of widespread large, crusted, ulcerative skin lesions accompanied by intense headache, fever, myalgia, and leukorrhea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the preceding month, the patient developed multiple large, rupioid, crusted ulcerative lesions over her face, trunk, and extremities, accompanied by fever, severe headache, myalgia, and vaginal discharge, without any preceding primary genital chancre.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of two untreated spontaneous miscarriages. Married to a truck driver with multiple premarital and extramarital sexual contacts who had been diagnosed with HIV 2 years earlier (on ART) and was concurrently being treated for genital ulcers/chancroid and found to have a positive VDRL (titer 1:64); the patient reported no sexual contact with her husband for the past 6 months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized crusted ulcerative skin lesions, oral/genital mucosal erosions, fever, intense headache, myalgia, and leukorrhea; negative for prior genital chancre.

objective.physical_examination: The patient was febrile. Cutaneous examination revealed multiple large ulcerative, rupioid-crusted lesions on the face and extremities, mucosal erosions on the lips and genitalia, and multiple annular plaques with central hyperpigmentation on the palms and soles. Lymphatic examination revealed enlarged, tender, rubbery axillary, epitrochlear, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. During healing, she exhibited classic leukoderma colli around the neck.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood tests showed polymorphonuclear leukocytosis and elevated ESR. HIV-1 ELISA and Western blot for p24 antigen were positive. Pus culture from the ulcerated skin lesions grew quinolone-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture CSF analysis showed normal opening pressure, normal cell count and protein, and a non-reactive CSF VDRL. Skin biopsy histopathology of a rupioid lesion demonstrated epidermal ulceration, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, a dense mid-dermal lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate, and obliterative endarteritis/vasculitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed malignant syphilis (lues maligna) with secondary S. aureus superinfection and newly diagnosed HIV-1 co-infection, established via high-titer serum VDRL (1:128), characteristic plasma-cell-rich obliterative vasculitis on skin biopsy, and partner VDRL positivity (1:64, treated with single-dose IM benzathine penicillin 2.4 million units). Because of her severe headache and fever, she was treated inpatient with intramuscular procaine penicillin 1.2 million units daily for 3 weeks plus oral fluoroquinolones for S. aureus, achieving complete healing of all cutaneous ulcers within 3 weeks, referral for HAART, and complete VDRL seroreversion (non-reactive VDRL, positive TPHA) at 6-month follow-up.
